publication_context.current_lean_module:
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.SemigroupDecay

/-!
# Forced energy-dissipation decay

This file extends the scalar semigroup-decay interface by allowing a constant
forcing term.  The result is the exact nonzero-forcing specialization of
Mathlib's one-sided Grönwall comparison: an energy satisfying
`E' ≤ -r E + b` approaches the floor `b / r` with exponential rate `r`.

Concrete semigroup construction, generator differentiation and curvature
estimates remain separate inputs.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory
namespace TechnicalLemmas
namespace FunctionalInequalities
namespace SemigroupDecay

open Filter Set
open scoped Topology

noncomputable section

/-- A forced coercive inequality gives an exponentially weighted interpolation
between the initial energy and the forcing floor.

The hypothesis
`rate * energy ≤ scale * dissipation + forcing`, together with
`energy' = -scale * dissipation`, is exactly the scalar differential
inequality `energy' ≤ -rate * energy + forcing`.  This form is useful when a
semigroup curvature estimate contains an additive error or when a dissipative
flow is driven by a bounded source. -/
theorem forced_exponential_decay_of_scaled_dissipation_from
    {scale rate forcing : ℝ} (hrate : 0 < rate)
    (curve : DissipationCurve scale)
    (hcoercive : ∀ u : ℝ,
      rate * curve.energy u ≤ scale * curve.dissipation u + forcing)
    {s t : ℝ} (hst : s ≤ t) :
    curve.energy t ≤
      curve.energy s * Real.exp (-rate * (t - s)) +
        (forcing / rate) * (1 - Real.exp (-rate * (t - s))) := by
  have hbound : ∀ x ∈ Ico s t,
      -scale * curve.dissipation x ≤
        (-rate) * curve.energy x + forcing := by
    intro x _hx
    have hneg := neg_le_neg (hcoercive x)
    linarith
  have hgronwall :=
    le_gronwallBound_of_liminf_deriv_right_le
      (f := curve.energy)
      (f' := fun x => -scale * curve.dissipation x)
      (δ := curve.energy s)
      (K := -rate)
      (ε := forcing)
      (a := s)
      (b := t)
      curve.energy_continuous.continuousOn
      (fun x _hx r hr => by
        simpa [slope] using
          (curve.energy_hasDerivWithinAt x).liminf_right_slope_le hr)
      le_rfl
      hbound
      t
      ⟨hst, le_rfl⟩
  rw [gronwallBound] at hgronwall
  simp only [if_neg (neg_ne_zero.mpr hrate.ne')] at hgronwall
  calc
    curve.energy t ≤
        curve.energy s * Real.exp (-rate * (t - s)) +
          forcing / -rate *
            (Real.exp (-rate * (t - s)) - 1) := hgronwall
    _ = curve.energy s * Real.exp (-rate * (t - s)) +
          (forcing / rate) *
            (1 - Real.exp (-rate * (t - s))) := by
      field_simp [hrate.ne']
      ring

end

end SemigroupDecay
end FunctionalInequalities
end TechnicalLemmas
end AutoSamplingTheory

source.attribution: Mathlib supplies the one-sided Grönwall comparison; Samplinglib packages the forced energy-dissipation specialization used by semigroup and optimization arguments.

publication_context.statement: For a continuous scalar energy with exact right derivative E'=-qD, a positive rate r and the inequality rE≤qD+b imply the sharp exponential interpolation E(t)≤E(s)e^{-r(t-s)}+(b/r)(1-e^{-r(t-s)}) for s≤t.
assumptions: The energy is continuous and has the supplied exact right derivative at every time.
The decay rate is strictly positive.
The forced coercivity inequality holds at every time.
The two endpoint times are ordered.

obligations.label: Derive the exact exponential envelope from right-derivative dissipation and forced coercivity

lesson.title: Dissipation with forcing converges to a floor
lesson.statement: Let an energy curve have the exact right derivative E'(u)=-qD(u). If r>0 and rE(u)≤qD(u)+b at every time, then between any s≤t the energy is bounded by the exponential interpolation between E(s) and the forcing floor b/r.
assumptions: The energy curve is continuous on the real line.
At each time u, its right derivative within [u,∞) is exactly -qD(u).
The decay rate r is strictly positive.
The forced coercivity inequality rE(u)≤qD(u)+b holds for every real u.

steps.title: Convert coercivity into a differential inequality
steps.text: Negating the forced coercivity inequality and using the derivative identity gives E'(u)≤-rE(u)+b.
steps.lean: The proof combines `neg_le_neg (hcoercive u)` with linear arithmetic.

steps.title: Apply one-sided Grönwall
steps.text: Mathlib's right-slope Grönwall theorem applies directly because the curve is continuous and the exact right derivative controls every right slope.

steps.title: Expose the forcing floor
steps.text: Since r is nonzero, unfold the closed Grönwall expression and rewrite b/(-r)(e^{-rΔ}-1) as (b/r)(1-e^{-rΔ}).
steps.lean: Unfold `gronwallBound`; `field_simp` and `ring` verify the scalar identity.

lesson.lean_statement: Lean keeps the dissipation scale q, decay rate r, forcing b, curve, and both endpoint times explicit.
lesson.lean_proof: The proof is a direct specialization of Mathlib's one-sided Grönwall theorem, followed by exact field algebra.
